summary: A 1932 L-4 lookout in the Payette National Forest was replaced in 1978 by an R-6 cab that still stands; it is generally staffed in fire season.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 10-foot concrete base (current cab); the first cab was an L-4 on a wooden base
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

access.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in and staffed; no source says whether visitors may climb the cab

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in; the sources give no route details

events.note: First L-4 cab on the site; the sources describe its base as log, log cribbing or enclosed timber
Earliest named lookout person: Glen Gwilliams on firelookout.com, spelled Glen Williams on idahofirelookouts.com
R-6 flat cab on a concrete base replaced the 1932 cab; the Register's Built field gives 1978

evidence.supports: about 15 miles northwest of New Meadows

evidence.quote: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

evidence.supports: established 1932 with L-4 cabin on enclosed timber tower; current R-6 cab built 1978
evidence.quote: Lick Creek Point Lookout was established in 1932 with an R1/L-4 cabin on an enclosed timber tower. The current structure, an R-6 flat cab was constructed in 1978.

evidence.supports: 1932 development with L-4 cab on log base; 1978 R-6 cab on concrete base; staffed in summer
evidence.quote: Developed in 1932, a 10' log base with L-4 cab was replaced in 1978 by an R-6 flat cab atop a 10' concrete base, which is staffed in the summer.
1932: A L-4 cab atop a first floor of log cribbing.

evidence.supports: 1978 current R-6 cab on block tower
evidence.quote: 1978: Current R-6 on block tower constructed

corrections.proposed: 1932 (first L-4 cab); 1978 (current R-6 cab replaced it)
corrections.why: The Register's Built field gives 1978, but the Register's own description and firelookout.com date the site's first cab to 1932.

corrections.proposed: remove (no source gives total tower height)
corrections.why: The only related figure in the sources is a 10-foot concrete base, about 3.05 m. That base is the likely source of 3.0, not a total tower height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1978 date is the current R-6 cab; the 1932 date is the first L-4 cab on the site. Both are recorded as separate events.
The first base is called a log base, log cribbing or an enclosed timber tower. All three describe wood, so the story describes it as wooden.

notes_for_editor: Watchman spelling (Gwilliams on firelookout.com, Williams on idahofirelookouts.com) is unresolved. The newest source is the 2020 Register entry, so current staffing and condition are unconfirmed. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is dropped from facts pending editor sign-off. No photos added.
